title: mashwrapper pipeline parameters
description: This is a wrapper around the program Mash. The input is a mash database and your fastq reads of interest. The output is a text file which displays the top five closet matches to your query.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

email_addy.description: Primary email address to send the results summary file

email_cc.description: Email addresses to CC when sending results (comma-separated if multiple)

email_subject.default: Results from mashWrapper for identifying species
email_subject.description: Custom subject line for the results email

input.description: Path to CSV file containing information about the samples in the experiment and has the following header:   sample,fastq1.gz,fastq2.gz
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: Path to the output directory where results will be saved

assembly_level.description: Restrict genomes downloaded to specific assembly levels: chromosome, complete, scaffold, contig (comma-separated list)

get_database.description: Path to a plain text file listing organisms to download from NCBI; one per line, as either "Genus" or "Genus species"

use_database.description: Path to a prebuilt Mash database (.msh)

kmer_min.description: Minimum k-mer copy number. Defaults to estimated coverage/3; override with a custom value ≥ 2

max_dist.description: Maximum Mash distance to consider for species identification

num_threads.description: Number of threads to use for parallel processing

size_kmer.description: Length of k-mers used in Mash sketches (1–32). Only applicable when downloading genomes or inferred from prebuilt database

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime
